areas.why: NHS income 4030 is booked at the full 1,020,000 (12 x 85,000 receipts) although Raj expects about 92% UDA delivery for 2025/26. NHS England claws back the shortfall, so Apr-Dec 2025 income is overstated by about 61,200 (8% x 9/12 x 1,020,000; 81,600 for the whole contract year), roughly 2.5x overall materiality. Private card takings (649,143, up exactly 12%) are keyed in weekly by Sue from the practice management system, there is no W52 takings entry for 22-31 Dec, and a director posted the one manual revenue debit himself.

No clawback provision has been made (N4); the estimate is c.61k against PM of 18k, and the last clawback was about 40k. The ledger as exported on 6 Mar 2026 contains none of Moorland's year-end journals: accruals of 4,100 have not moved since the prior year, 2260 provisions is nil, 7601 audit fee is nil in both years, and there is no corporation tax charge or liability in either year (pre-tax profit is c.563.6k), nor any CT payment in the 2025 bank.

This is an owner-managed company with no segregation of duties: Sue posts and approves 353 of the 373 purchase invoices and approves the payroll import, and Raj posted MJ-000013 (a 1,900 debit to revenue and credit to bank) at 18:40 with no approver. Management's attitude to the clawback estimate ('Moorland usually do that') points to possible bias. All the year-end journals are still to be posted, by an outside party acting on Sue's instructions.

Sue posts and approves every invoice under 5,000 (FY24-W03, which relied on a compensating control), and last year a duplicate invoice was found (FY24-W01). In the ledger, descriptions do not fit the suppliers: Moorland bills 'Indemnity' and 'CQC registration', Dental Protection bills 'Payroll bureau' while Sue runs payroll in-house (N6), and Practice Growth Marketing bills 13 'CPD/conference travel' items coded to 7400. Associate invoices from Dr Farooq ('45% of private fees - monthly') are missing for Jan, Apr and Jul-Oct, which could be up to about 40-60k of unrecorded subcontractor cost.

Ten payees, all on the HR list with no leavers, and the net pay in all 12 months agrees to the individual bank payments (10 lines per month summing to 23,199). The cost is identical every month (gross 31,350, employer's NI 3,448.50, a flat 11.0%), with no change from April 2025 when the employer NIC rate and threshold changed, so accuracy needs recomputing. The SoD weakness (N6) is mitigated by my bank-to-HR matching.

There is one budgeted addition, the Surgery 2 chair (45,600; invoice PI-000373 approved by Raj, paid 2 Jun at B25-00230). Depreciation is posted by Sue (not Moorland) at a flat 2,200 a month, so nothing was charged on the chair after May (total 26,400 = PY). This is likely an understatement of about 2.7-5.3k, below PM but above the clearly trivial threshold.

All 570 lines on the 2025 statement match the ledger once payroll is netted, and the closing statement balance of 643,933 agrees to TB 1200. The float is 200. The Q1 2026 statement runs only to 9 Feb and has no NHS receipts, no takings and no January payroll, so it is incomplete or there has been an event. I need the full statement, but this does not raise the risk on the balance itself.

The two 50% director-shareholders are paid through payroll only (4,810 net each per month). There is no director loan account and no dividends in the ledger, and the landlord is stated to be unconnected. Open points: directors' travel/CPD billed through a marketing supplier, whether the largest supplier (Wetherby Dental Laboratory, 145.7k) is connected, and the absence of any dividends despite the cash build-up.

The company is cash-rich (643,933 against creditors of 36,163 plus PAYE of 11,600), has no borrowing and makes a pre-tax profit of c.564k. The NHS contract runs until it ends and the lease runs to 2031. The only open question is the incomplete Q1 2026 statement with no receipts.

There are no trade debtors: NHS pays monthly and private patients pay at reception, so the debtors balance is nil in both years. There are no prepayments or other debtors in the TB at all, although indemnity instalments and rent might call for some. This is low risk and limited to other debtors and prepayments.

Last year's plan treated the practice as exempt and not registered, but the Q1 2026 bank statement shows 'HMRC VAT - VAT Q4 2025 - VAT return' for 0.00 (B26-00028). That suggests a registration, possibly nil returns, which would bring VAT-01 into scope. Every ledger line is coded T2 or T9 with no VAT. Low monetary risk, but the registration status needs confirming.

This is a continuing engagement (6th year) with an unmodified prior-year opinion, and the opening TB equals the PY closing. Even so, the PY comparative column looks unusual: every P&L line moves by an exact round percentage (0/2/5/8/10/12/30/60%), and utilities, travel, professional fees, bank charges and depreciation are identical to the penny. The comparatives should be agreed to the signed FY2024 accounts. OB-01 does not apply.

No stock is recognised in the chart of accounts and consumables are expensed to 5030. The one caveat is the new implant service, so confirm that implant components held at the year end are not material.

The clawback outcome becomes known after the year end: the 2025/26 reconciliation is due after 31 Mar 2026 and the clawback is usually in July. The year-end journals are still outstanding and the Q1 2026 statement is incomplete. Subsequent events and the regulatory work (NHS contract, CQC) carry more than normal weight this year.

keyFindings: NHS income is booked at 100% of the 1,020,000 contract (12 x 85,000) despite expected UDA delivery of about 92%. The unprovided clawback for Apr-Dec 2025 is c.61.2k (81.6k for the full contract year), about 2.5x overall materiality and 3.4x PM. No provision exists (N4, TB 2260 nil).

The ledger as exported on 6 Mar 2026 has no year-end adjustments. There is no corporation tax charge or liability in either FY2024 or FY2025 and no CT payment in the 2025 bank, the audit fee is nil in both years, and the 4,100 accrual is unchanged. Pre-tax profit is c.563.6k, so CT alone would be about 140k.

Dr Farooq's associate fees ('45% of private fees - monthly') were invoiced in only 7 of 12 months (none in Jan, Apr or Jul-Oct), giving possible unrecorded subcontractor costs of tens of thousands. Subcontractors are still up 30%.

Invoice descriptions do not fit the suppliers in Sue's self-approved population: Moorland bills 'Indemnity'/'CQC registration', Dental Protection bills 'Payroll bureau' even though payroll is run in-house, and Practice Growth Marketing bills 13 'CPD/conference travel' items. This suggests misclassification or invoices that need vouching.

Payroll cost is identical every month with employer's NI at a flat 11.0%, and there is no step change in April 2025 when employer NIC rose to 15% and the threshold fell to 5,000. Gross pay and employer's NI each move by exactly 5% on PY.
Every P&L line moves by an exact round percentage and five lines equal PY to the penny (including bank charges of 642.35). The comparatives should be agreed to the signed FY2024 accounts.

The Q1 2026 bank statement ends on 9 Feb and contains no NHS receipts, no takings and no January payroll. It includes a nil 'VAT return Q4 2025' line, which contradicts the PY 'not VAT registered' note.

The bank reconciles fully: all 570 2025 statement lines match the ledger, with closing 643,933 equal to TB 1200, and all 10 payees agree to the HR list. Depreciation on the 45,600 chair has not been charged.

hoursEstimateVsBudget: About 90 hours against a 60-hour budget (+30h, +50%). FY2024 was budgeted at 67h with 50h actual. The excess is risk-driven: REV-04 (10h), REV-03 (3h), REV-06 (5h), PUR-03 (4h), extended JNL-01/JNL-02/ACC-01 (+6h) and a conditional VAT-01 (3h). Breakdown: revenue 25, debtors 2, purchases 19, payroll 5, FA 2, bank 5, RP 3, journals 18, GC 2, VAT 3 (conditional), accruals 5, completion 5.
